content_metadata.description: Doug Cutting reflects on the values and experiences associated with the Apache Software Foundation.

qAndA.answer: A diverse group of people working together to build something.
qAndA.question: What is the key requirement of the ASF according to Doug Cutting?

qAndA.answer: The ability to be honest and focus on building good software without the pressure of self-promotion.
qAndA.question: What does Doug Cutting find liberating about the ASF compared to the commercial world?
What value does Apache not prioritize?

qAndA.answer: He believes it's a better way of building software.
qAndA.question: How does Doug Cutting describe the ASF's approach to software development?

qAndA.answer: His genuine smile when he talks about the liberating aspect of honesty within the ASF.
qAndA.question: What aspect of Doug Cutting's delivery suggests sincerity in his belief about the ASF?

characterInteraction.description: Doug Cutting speaks directly to the viewer.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Doug's words critique the competitive and less transparent nature of the commercial software industry, highlighting core values of open source development.

narrativeProgression.description: Doug shares his initial lack of knowledge about the Apache Software Foundation (ASF).
He highlights the ASF's key requirement: a diverse group of people collaborating on a project.
Doug emphasizes the liberating nature of honesty within the ASF, contrasting it with the commercial world's emphasis on self-promotion.
He emphasizes the ASF's focus on building good software rather than seeking personal glory.

scenes.thematicElements: Open source software development, collaboration, honesty, focus on quality over personal gain.
scenes.title: Doug Cutting's Perspective on ASF

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: When I came to the ASF originally, I didn't know anything about it.
About the only thing it requires is a diverse group of people to work together to build something.
Being honest is a wonderfully liberating thing to do coming from the commercial world where
you're always trying to convince people that what you're doing is better and it's the
best. The value of Apache is that it's not seeking glory and not demanding glory.
Really do believe it's a better way of building software.

youtube_description: Interview with ASF Member and Apache Hadoop and Lucene projects creator Doug Cutting on his experiences with Apache. The all-volunteer, Apache Software Foundation (ASF), develops more than 100 freely-available, Open Source projects used by billions of users each day. Join us in celebrating the ASFs 10th anniversary 2-6 November at ApacheCon, featuring the largest conference program to date, including a number of free events open to the public in appreciation of their support over the past decade. Register today at http://www.us.apachecon.com/
